liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (3 reviews): Jerry hits hard in the first solo of the opener; Brent uses some deep, buzzing keyboard sounds in this version [28][29][35]
- **Drums** (1 review): At the end of Drums, Mickey and Billy set an offbeat, Bobby follows, and Jerry joins in [34]
- **The Other One** (1 review): About five minutes of sweet jamming, then Other One teases, then it builds gradually with pauses into the song [34]
- **Mexicali Blues** (1 review): Played at a fast tempo, with tasteful short Jerry solos, following Me & My Uncle [26]

## Setlist highlights

- **Other Jam**: back after 379 archived shows (1804 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [37]
- **Other Jam**: back after 379 archived shows (1804 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [37]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-04-16.176982.senn.md241.strizak.fix.flac2448** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 147 min [1]. Said about its sound: Strizak applied some EQ to tame bass boom and some high frequencies [1]
- **gd1984-04-16.senn441.koucky.ladner.fix-32884.35408.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 144 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [7]
- **gd1984-04-16.164731.senn441.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 155 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [11]
- **gd84-04-16.neumann.1298.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 148 min; rated 4.29/5 by 14 [13]. Said about its sound: Audience recording described as excellent, though the reviewer would like somewhat more low-end response [26]

## Around the show

- Reviewer, stationed at RAF Lakenheath in England, got tickets for spring tour and drove from Albany to Rochester with friends [25]
- Reviewer says this was their first Grateful Dead show [33]
- Reviewer's brother was introduced to the Grateful Dead at this show [35]
- Reviewer got a flat tire en route, sat near two young kids, and shared a bottle of Jack [36]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-04-16.176982.senn.md241.strizak.fix.flac2448**: taped by Taped by and transferred/mastered by Tom Strizak April 2026; source: Tom Strizak Master Audience Cassettes (2 TDK-MA90 / Dolby OFF). (2) Sennheiser MD421 standard stereo configuration (mic stand at approx. 6’) Sony TC-D5M stereo… [1]. Also: Tom Strizak corrected a left-heavy channel balance caused in Audacity; this upgrades source 176954 [1]
- **gd1984-04-16.senn441.koucky.ladner.fix-32884.35408.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Bill Koucky; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: FOB Sennheiser 441s > Sony D5 > D5 > MAC [7]. Also: Bill Tetzeli lowered the pitch with a 101.86% time/pitch stretch in CE Pro; Starts of Shakedown Street and Me and My Uncle were patched from the Neumann U-87 recording with crossfades [7]
- **gd1984-04-16.164731.senn441.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) Sennheiser 441 mics + (1) Neumann U87 mic blend > Nakamichi 550 [11]. Also: Doug Lamarre's Sennheiser 441 source supplies a 17-second patch in Drums; the Other One space is included in The Other One [11]
- **gd84-04-16.neumann.1298.sbeok.shnf**: source: Neumann U-87 > Sony d-6 >dat >cdr [13]

Grateful Dead Community War Memorial - April 16, 1984

claims.text: Reviewer, stationed at RAF Lakenheath in England, got tickets for spring tour and drove from Albany to Rochester with friends
Played at a fast tempo, with tasteful short Jerry solos, following Me & My Uncle
Audience recording described as excellent, though the reviewer would like somewhat more low-end response
Jerry hits hard in the first solo of the opener
Brent uses some deep, buzzing keyboard sounds in this version
The ending of the song is called trippy
Loose and torn apart, then the final vocal section lifts it into a top-20 version
Reviewer says this was their first Grateful Dead show
At the end of Drums, Mickey and Billy set an offbeat, Bobby follows, and Jerry joins in
About five minutes of sweet jamming, then Other One teases, then it builds gradually with pauses into the song
Opening Shakedown Street is called one of the best the reviewer has heard
Reviewer's brother was introduced to the Grateful Dead at this show
Reviewer got a flat tire en route, sat near two young kids, and shared a bottle of Jack
Tom Strizak corrected a left-heavy channel balance caused in Audacity; this upgrades source 176954
Strizak applied some EQ to tame bass boom and some high frequencies
Bill Tetzeli lowered the pitch with a 101.86% time/pitch stretch in CE Pro
Starts of Shakedown Street and Me and My Uncle were patched from the Neumann U-87 recording with crossfades
Rob Eaton made the recording; Charlie Miller coordinated the transfer, and the source is a Sennheiser 441 and Neumann U-87 blend
Doug Lamarre's Sennheiser 441 source supplies a 17-second patch in Drums; the Other One space is included in The Other One
